neighbours.label: the slot right before a word naming an effect, hazard or property in health and science writing (used for its [stimulant] properties, even more [harmful])
fire: Nicotine is valued by smokers for its calming effect.
Lead in drinking water is especially dangerous to children.
The new drug had little effect on blood pressure.
Ozone at ground level is far more toxic than people think.
Alcohol is a depressant that slows the nervous system.
Regular exercise has a strong protective effect on the heart.
These pesticides pose a serious risk to bees.
Some herbs are taken for their sedative properties.
quiet: Nicotine was first isolated from tobacco in 1828.
Lead pipes were common in houses built before 1950.
The new drug was approved in Canada last spring.
Ozone is a molecule made of three oxygen atoms.
Alcohol is sold in most supermarkets in the city.
Regular exercise classes are held in the town hall.
These pesticides are sold in large plastic drums.
Some herbs are grown in pots on the windowsill.

notes: card/look: psychoactive (, morphine's effects, a special health hazard, for their stimulant properties, had no effect, even more harmful. Output suppresses beneficial/harmful (the - pole promotes them).
